budget_items.topic: Speculative market pricing of new town house units (Brackett proposal)
budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant's engineer said a developer could market units at one price and a later owner could resell for far more since pricing is market-driven, not fixed by the permit.

budget_items.topic: Affordable-unit price threshold under the town's inclusionary bylaw
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident recalled that affordable units under the bylaw had to be priced around a percentage of area cost, though he was unsure if that had changed.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to leave a traffic study requirement to the Planning Board's review rather than requiring one itself before deciding on the Brackett special permit.
Board and applicant agreed to condition the Brackett permit on additional visitor parking (one extra space per unit) rather than a specific parking layout, to be worked out with the Planning Board.

public_comment.topic: Asked who is responsible for snow plowing on the proposed common driveway, whether the driveway would be wide enough, and whether a pro forma had been prepared to gauge likely home prices and affordability; suggested the application might be premature given how much remains to be determined.

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 833 New West Townsend Road (Fitchburg side), abutter across the street
public_comment.topic: Said the proposed density of five units per lot is far greater than the surrounding neighborhood, raised concerns about effects on property values, doubted there is enough water in the area to support fire sprinklers or wells, and flagged a sharp, narrow corner near the proposed driveway as a safety hazard.

public_comment.stated_role: abutting property owner, owner of the old Lahree/Pierce's Tree Farm property
public_comment.topic: Raised concerns about hillside erosion running onto his property during construction, citing the earlier O'Brien project, and said the site's water table may not support the proposed density.
Described the existing school bus stop location at the corner of Howard Street and New West Townsend Road and said children from the new units would have to walk a long way to reach it.
Explained, from her experience driving buses for the district, how bus routing and turnarounds work on New West Townsend Road and that the bus company would handle any new stop.

minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard two special permit applications. It granted Matthew Glenny a special permit with a dimensional variance to build a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit at 55 Valley Road, subject to septic upgrades being worked out with the Board of Health. It then heard and voted to approve, with added conditions on driveway width and extra parking, a special permit allowing Daniel and Rachel Brackett to build four five-unit town house buildings off a common driveway on New West Townsend Road, over objections from several neighbors about density, traffic, water supply for fire suppression, and erosion.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for Matthew Glenny's garage/ADU with the dimensional variations as requested, provided all boards are accommodated per their procedures.

Approve the Brackett special permit for the town house development, conditioned on the common driveway being at least 20 feet wide and one additional parking space per unit beyond the bylaw-required amount.
votes.outcome: passed, with one apparent dissenting voice heard; exact count not audible

what_happened.line: The board approved a special permit for four five-unit town house buildings off a common driveway on New West Townsend Road, over neighbor objections.
The board granted a special permit with a dimensional variance for a detached garage with an accessory dwelling unit at 55 Valley Road, pending septic upgrades with the Board of Health.
The board left the question of whether a traffic study is needed to the Planning Board's later review rather than requiring one before its own vote.
The town house approval was conditioned on a common driveway at least 20 feet wide and one extra parking space per unit.

why_it_matters: Approves higher-density housing on New West Townsend Road; residents raised unresolved questions about water supply for fire suppression, driveway safety, and construction erosion that now move to the Planning Board's review rather than being settled here.
Sets a precedent for granting dimensional variances for accessory dwelling units, a housing type the town may see more requests for.
The septic and driveway conditions mean neither project is fully resolved -- Board of Health and Planning Board sign-off remain outstanding steps.
